deep.reconstruction:
Goal: find the constant in the prime sum sum_{p<x} log p/(p-1) = log x + B + o(1). The method compares the behaviour of Dirichlet series as s->1+ with the behaviour of partial sums as x->infinity (an Abelian argument).

Step A. Near s=1, zeta(s) = sum n^{-s} = 1/(s-1) + gamma + o(1).

Step B. -zeta'(s) = sum log n / n^s = 1/(s-1)^2 + K + o(1). Ramanujan leaves K unnamed. In modern terms K = -gamma_1, the first Stieltjes constant; the next page makes this explicit.

Step C. Dividing gives -zeta'/zeta = [1/(s-1)^2 + K]/[1/(s-1) + gamma] = (1/(s-1))(1 + K(s-1)^2)(1 - gamma(s-1) + ...) = 1/(s-1) - gamma + O(s-1). The value of K drops out.

Step D. By the Euler product, -zeta'/zeta(s) = sum Lambda(n) n^{-s} = sum_p log p sum_{k>=1} p^{-ks} = sum_p log p/(p^s - 1). (The symbol ≡ is used for this identity.) Hence sum_p log p/(p^s-1) = 1/(s-1) - gamma + o(1).

Step E, eq (1). Subtracting from Step A: zeta(s) - sum_p log p/(p^s-1) = 2 gamma + o(1).

Step F, eq (2). sum_{n<x} 1/n = log x + gamma + o(1).

Step G, eq (3). Assuming the prime number theorem pi(x) ~ x/log x, sum_{p<x} log p/(p-1) = log x + B + o(1) for some constant B.

Step H [implicit, mine]. Abelian lemma: if sum_{n<=x} a_n/n = log x + C + o(1), then sum a_n n^{-s} = 1/(s-1) + C + o(1) as s->1+. Proof sketch: write A(x) = log x + C + eps(x); then sum a_n n^{-s} = (s-1) int_1^inf A(x) x^{-s} dx = 1/(s-1) + C + (s-1) int eps x^{-s} dx, and the last term tends to 0.
- Applied to (2), this gives zeta(s) = 1/(s-1) + gamma + o(1).
- Applied to (3), with a_p = p log p/(p-1), it gives sum_p log p/(p^s-1) = 1/(s-1) + B + o(1). The difference between sum p log p/((p-1)p^s) and sum log p/(p^s-1) is o(1) as s->1.
- Subtracting, the left side of (1) tends to gamma - B. So gamma - B = 2 gamma, i.e. B = -gamma.

Conclusion: log2/1 + log3/2 + log5/4 + log7/6 + ... + log p/(p-1) (over p<x) = log x - gamma + o(1). Equivalently sum_{n<=x} Lambda(n)/n = log x - gamma + o(1).

The next page runs the identical scheme for sum d(n)/n, using gamma_1.
errors: No outright error; the final result is correct.

The existence of the limit B in (3) does not follow trivially from pi(x) ~ x/log x. Mertens (1874) gives only log x + O(1) unconditionally. The o(1) form is a known consequence of the PNT and in fact equivalent to it (Landau 1909). Ramanujan states it as an assumption without proof, and the Abelian matching determines B only once the limit is known to exist.

The Abelian step (Dirichlet-series constant equals partial-sum constant) is used implicitly. Strictly, the series in (1), sum log p/(p^s-1), is not literally the Dirichlet series whose s=1 partial sums appear in (3). The discrepancy is o(1) as s->1, so this is harmless.
K is left undetermined, which is legitimate since it cancels. Its true value is -gamma_1 = -0.0728158...

deep.surprise_reason: The result sum log p/(p-1) = log x - gamma + o(1) is a known consequence of the PNT (Landau 1909), and the constant-matching argument is standard. The page is a clean heuristic derivation, typical of Ramanujan, assuming the PNT. These Trinity manuscripts on gamma and prime sums have, I believe, been discussed by Andrews-Berndt (Lost Notebook IV), but I am unsure. Nothing here is new to the literature.
